lxc_c3cd4d4ca7d16f6b.text: Today we will learn who the Japanese gods are and how people honour them.

lxc_215a214bdc985739.text: We will read four famous myths and see what each one teaches.

lxc_bbec4bf9e4b885d0.text: Most come from the Kojiki (古事記), *Records of Ancient Matters*, finished in 712.

lxc_384d5b8342772801.text: The way of honouring the kami is called Shinto (神道), *the way of the gods*.

lxc_806d3704b7e474d9.text: Because kami are everywhere in nature, people speak of yaoyorozu no kami (八百万の神).

lxc_5614b955f0e02518.text: Kami are believed to hate anything dirty.

lxc_8eda44726068d832.text: Then they drop a coin into the offering box, bow twice, clap twice and bow once more.

lxc_28b6ffed2ea74fa3.text: In front of these things, people feel great respect and a little fear.

lxc_921afcaa0086b652.text: So visitors first purify themselves: they wash their hands and mouth with water at a stone basin.

lxc_9aad095bfe4c2489.text: Examples are a high mountain, a waterfall, a very old tree, the sun and the spirits of ancestors.

lxc_6f9a4f606501ac7d.text: Priests also give the kami offerings of food they like, such as rice, sake and salt.

lxc_e1c75b3c9a794dd1.text: Where do the stories of the kami come from?

lxc_a012f109e58d2191.text: Three of the four stories in this lesson come from there.

lxc_268153c1b0b1f137.text: In Japanese, a god is called a kami (神).

lxc_62f420dcae77d810.text: Anything with a strong, special power can be a kami.

lxc_bb222e5f30895379.text: At the entrance stands a torii (鳥居), a gate that is often painted red.

lxc_5eb045ee6f41845f.text: The torii marks a line: outside is the everyday world, and inside is the sacred home of the kami.

lxc_62f4145a82e85faa.text: It is made of two posts and two long pieces of wood across the top.

lxc_11a9b270496e2181.text: People honour kami at a shrine, or jinja (神社).

lxc_15a02175deaa912d.text: But a kami is not only a person in the sky.

lxc_562348ea329023d7.text: The Kojiki has three books, and the first one tells the myths of the kami.

lxc_271b4972c5db45ef.text: It is the oldest book in Japan that still exists.
